body.estimand_functional: \(\theta_B\in[L(p_Q),U(p_Q)]=\left[\sum_xF_L\{H_x(p_Q)\}/M(p_Q),\sum_xF_U\{H_x(p_Q)\}/M(p_Q)\right]\), by the imported AcceptedSlateBenefit2026 sharp-endpoint theorem

sampling_model.design: For each \(n\), observe an independent sample \(O_{n1},\ldots,O_{nn}\) from the row law \(P_n\in\mathcal M\); rows may vary arbitrarily with \(n\).
sampling_model.units: The number of multinomial atoms \(|\mathcal J|\) is fixed, while their probabilities may vanish with \(n\).
sampling_model.treatment: The instrument and treatment are binary; the outcome has the fixed ordered support \(\mathcal Y\), and selection is observed.
sampling_model.overlap: The inferential class strengthens the inherited pointwise model only by fixed uniform bounds \(\epsilon\le P_n(Z=1\mid X=x)\le1-\epsilon\) and \(M(p_n)\ge m_*\); individual cells and cut gaps may vanish.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The empirical atom vector \(\widehat p_n\) is the sole first-stage estimator. Algebraic division is totalized by \(u\oslash0=0\), the endpoint center uses \(\Phi_{\mathrm{ext}}(\widehat p_n)=(0,1)\) at zero aggregate empirical mass, and \(C_n=\mathbb R^2\) when that fallback is invoked or the legal base set is empty. The common Gaussian draw is realized through the principal covariance square root, and its measurable critical value uses the lower-quantile convention. No support screening, variance floor, or deterministic calibration guard is used.

body.tldr: The accepted \(\text{pid\_slate\_benefit\_partialtransport}\) theorem supplies the sharp probability-of-benefit interval among survivor compliers as a ratio of finite capacity extrema; identification is therefore substrate, not a new result. The inferential proposal totalizes every capacity ratio and directional derivative, derives finite Borel legal-base envelopes, and calibrates both endpoint errors with one measurable conditional Gaussian max norm, using a full-plane fallback whenever the legal base set is empty or aggregate empirical mass is zero. Its theorem-level target is uniform joint coverage without lower bounds on individual survivor cells, cut gaps, or endpoint variances; exact bivariate-Gaussian calibration is recovered on separated regular faces, and width is \(O_P(n^{-1/2})\) on root-\(n\) support-emergence and tied-cut arrays. The unresolved mathematical core is a legal observed-law inner-neighborhood comparison combined with relative critical-value transfer when the entire envelope scale vanishes.

project_justification.gap: The accepted parent settles sharp identification for the finite ordered survivor-complier benefit interval. Existing inference results either impose fixed-law differentiability, start from supplied asymptotically linear endpoint or standardized moment representations, or require geometric and positive-variance regularity that excludes changing support and a jointly collapsing endpoint scale.
project_justification.niche: The finite binary-instrument model permits exact capacity geometry and multinomial coupling, yet legality of nearby observed laws is more restrictive than ambient perturbation of a probability vector. This creates a tractable model-specific route to uniform inference at zero cells and tied extrema.
project_justification.fill: The total legal-base envelope retains every nearby support and cut face, uses one Gaussian draw for both endpoints, and seeks a scale-homogeneous comparison yielding honest coverage over all legal triangular arrays while reverting to the exact oracle rectangle on separated faces.

body.related_work: The accepted CausalSmith result pid\_slate\_benefit\_partialtransport, Theorem thm:sharp-exact-mass-threshold-interval, is imported verbatim as the identification substrate: it proves the exact endpoint formula and full-law sharpness under the inherited finite covariate, finite ordered outcome, binary-instrument selection model. Angrist, Imbens, and Rubin (1996) support conditional instrument randomization, treatment consistency, and global no-defiers; Dong and Heiler (2026), Assumptions 3.1--3.2, support treatment-mediated selection and outcome consistency together with covariate-specific weak selection monotonicity. The fixed \(\epsilon\) overlap bound and fixed \(m_*\) aggregate denominator floor are strengthened uniform-class restrictions here, not claims attributed to Kennedy, Harris, and Keele (2019). Kennedy, Harris, and Keele define survivor-complier mean effects and provide fixed-law efficient inference, so their work informs the population and inferential comparison only. Gabriel, Sachs, and Jensen (2024) derive sharp symbolic ordinal benefit bounds and identify confidence intervals at boundaries as an open inferential issue. Fang and Santos (2019) show why ordinary bootstrap inference fails for nonlinear directional derivatives and motivate resampling the derivative itself. Hong and Li (2018) approximate directional derivatives numerically, with uniform validity for convex Lipschitz maps under additional Gaussian-boundary conditions. Frandsen and Pond (2025) calibrate common rectangles when endpoint estimators already possess a joint asymptotically normal representation. Imai and Okamoto (2026), Theorems 1--2 and Assumptions 1 and 5, establish uniformly valid multiplier-bootstrap bands for infinite-dimensional interval-valued parameters from supplied uniformly asymptotically linear endpoint estimators and Gaussian-process variances bounded away from zero; those conditions do not construct the legal observed-law derivative of this changing rational capacity map and rule out a jointly collapsing endpoint scale. Andrews and Guggenberger (2009), Theorems 1--2 and equation (3.3), prove uniform validity for subsampling and plug-in procedures built from standardized moment-inequality statistics with positive component variances; that representation neither realizes capacity directions inside the legal causal-law image nor supplies relative calibration when all endpoint variation vanishes. Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2022) demonstrate that the geometric qualifications behind partial-identification inference are substantive and model-specific. Voronin (2025) gives pointwise LP-value inference and proves that unrestricted uniform consistency is impossible, motivating exploitation of the survivor model's special legal geometry. Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, Kato, and Koike (2022), Lopes, Lin, and Müller (2020), and Vijaykumar (2026) inform the Gaussian-max comparison, but do not provide relative critical-value transfer when the entire scale collapses. Duarte, Finkelstein, Knox, Mummolo, and Shpitser (2024) center legal discrete causal laws in sharp-bound computation; the present target is the distinct local legal perturbation theorem required for inference.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The finite unconditional-capacity reduction, legal tangent-domain result, definable measurability result, regular-face oracle calculation, tight critical-value argument, and explicit \(K=4\) legal array do not prove \(\text{oeq:legal-relative-comparison}\). Algebraic values \(d_b(g)\) for \(g\notin\mathcal D_b\) make optimization total but provide no ambient-to-legal lift. Even on \(\mathcal D_b\), the capacity direction required for domination must still be realized by nearby legal observed laws, and additive weak-convergence error is insufficient when the common critical radius vanishes. The total procedure is defined on every sample: \(\Phi_{\mathrm{ext}}=(0,1)\) at zero empirical aggregate mass and \(C_n=\mathbb R^2\) there or when \(B_n\) is empty. A reproducible coverage deficit or persistent legal-versus-ambient mismatch beyond the certified \(\text{prop:k4-kill-test}\) array stops the proposed construction.
body.honest_scope: Sharp identification is imported from AcceptedSlateBenefit2026 and is not a contribution of this proposal. Treatment-indexed selection and outcomes are inherited structural definitions; conditional IV randomization, treatment consistency, and no-defiers follow the Angrist--Imbens--Rubin IV model, while weak selection monotonicity follows Dong--Heiler. Fixed \(\epsilon\) overlap and fixed \(m_*\) aggregate survivor mass are strengthened uniform-class conditions. Total algebraic division, the off-domain derivative convention, and the full-plane branch make the statistic finite and measurable; off-domain values do not assert a legal tangent lift. The regular-face theorem, root-\(n\) width, and explicit atom-level \(K=4\) diagnostic have direct proof traction. Uniform joint coverage remains conditional on resolving the legal inner-neighborhood and collapsing-scale relative-transfer question. No lower bound on an individual cell probability, cut gap, or endpoint variance is introduced. Under a fixed separated law, the proposal reduces to the standard bivariate multinomial delta method and its exact Gaussian max-norm critical value.
